utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be seated. Registrar, what is the number of the case that we are dealing with today?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is IT-95-4-I. The Prosecutor of the Tribunal against Zeljko Meakic, Miroslav Kvocka, Dragoljub Prcac, Mladen Radic aka "Krkan", Milojica Kos aka "Krle", Momcilo Gruban aka "Ckalja", Zdravko Govedarica, Gruban, Predrag Kostic aka "Kole," Nedeljko Paplalj, Milan Pavlic, Milutin Popovic, Drazenko Predojevic, Zeljko Savic, Mirko Babic, Nikica Janjic, Dusan Knezevic aka "Duca", Dragomir Saponja, Zoran Zigic aka "Ziga".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It is Mr. Zoran Zigic, alias Ziga, who is here today. That is that he will be here as soon as we ask him to be brought into the courtroom. Can we have the security guards have Mr. Zoran Zigic brought into the courtroom? That is Zoran Zigic, alias Ziga

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The photographer can withdraw now. I will ask Mr. Zoran Zigic, first, whether he hears me. Mr. Zigic, do you hear me? I ask you to please rise and to state your name, your given names and your date and place of birth, your profession and your last place of domicile.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIGIC
utterances.text: My name is Zoran Zigic, born on 20th September 1958 in Prijedor, by occupation a driver, my last domicile Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you need to wear those dark glasses? Are you wearing them for medical reasons, or is it for other reasons? THE DEFENDANT: Yes, I have very sensitive eyes to the light.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I, therefore, do not think that there would be any problems for the judges for you to wear those glasses. All right, you may wear the dark glasses. Since you are still standing, Mr. Zigic, first you might tell us who your attorney or attorneys are. I know one of them, but I would like you to tell us yourself. Who are your two counsellors, the two you have chosen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIGIC
utterances.text: Mr. Fila, and I am not quite sure of the surname, and Ms. Lopicic. They are my counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I believe we know this woman as well, she has been in this court before. For the Prosecutor, may I ask who is representing the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, your Honours. For the Prosecution, I am Michael Keegan and I am assisted today by my colleague, Ms. Ann Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zigic, you may be seated for the time being. Mr. Zigic, you are appearing for the first time before the International Criminal Tribunal. You are appearing pursuant to our Rules and the Statute which created this Tribunal, which was created by the Security Council of the Security Council and the provisions which are found not only in the Tribunal Statute but in the Rules of Evidence which were drafted further to that Statute. The provisions deal with the initial appearance and I would like to recall before you that there was one in the Statute which says that you must have the indictment read to you and that the Tribunal Chamber must be ensured that your rights have been completely respected and that you have understood the contents of the indictment before you plead guilty or not guilty. I believe that Mr. Fila or Ms. Lopicic have informed you of those provisions which are now well known within this Tribunal. Then, more specifically, as regards this hearing, there is Rule 62 in the Rules of Procedure and Evidence which repeat some of the provisions of the Statute, but which give more details. We will also be sure that you have the assistance of a counsel which you have named. We will read the indictment in a language which you understand, and then we will invite you to plead guilty or not guilty to each of the counts of the indictment. We will then finally see how we will organise our future work with certain specificities related to this case. In this case, I see two of them, as it relates to me, the first is that you appear in two indictments. I turn to my colleagues to see if they agree -- we will start with the first indictment which deals with the context of Mr. Meakic and others. I believe that is correct, is it not, Madam Registrar? That is the Omarska camp, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Then the second part, there may be a request for a joining of cases, but we will then ask the Prosecutor to speak to that matter later on. As regards the first case, that is the indictment -- do I have the version in French here, Madam Registrar? Yes, I do. This is the one which relates to the 13th February 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, that was indictment confirmed on 13th February 1995 by Judge Karibi-Whyte.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. This is the indictment which goes back to 1995. I will now turn to Mr. Fila. I do not know if he is the chief of the defence team, but I know he has experience in this case. Mr. Fila, has this indictment been given to Mr. Zigic and has Mr. Zigic understood the meaning of the indictment, even though we are going to reread it here?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I am sorry that I will appear only today. I had the pleasure to appear as Defence counsel in your Trial Chamber before. At the request of the Registry, I am standing in for an absent colleague from Banja Luka, who will be the actual Defence counsel of Mr. Zigic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: What is his name?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Mr. Tosic is his name. In the meantime, I have informed Mr. Zigic, with the indictment; he has read it; he understands it and there is no need for it to be read to him again. He is fully prepared to plead on all counts of the indictment, both regarding the first and the second indictment, depending on the wishes of the Prosecution and the Trial Chamber, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Nonetheless, we will read the indictment, at least we will take the mid point and read the relevant parts of the indictment. The Registrar has prepared her work in respect of this hearing. Therefore, she will read the indictment, but only those parts regarding this specific accused. We must read the entire general background. The Trial Chamber, despite the waiver on the part of the Defence to have the indictment read, the indictment should be read before this court and for the public. We will go to the 15 counts that were brought against this accused in 1995. After that, we will set up the practical measures and suspend the hearing and take a five-minute break to then read the second indictment. Madam Registrar, would you, please, read the indictment as we have agreed before this hearing?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The indictment confirmed on 13th February 1995. The Prosecutor of the Tribunal against Zeljko Meakic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: No, you do not have to read all that. You have read that already. That has been done already. This is an indictment which involves about 15 co-accused, including Mr. Zoran Zigic, alias Ziga. Therefore, please, begin with the part beginning with Mr. Goldstone.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Richard J Goldstone, Prosecutor of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia pursuant to his authority under Article 18 of the Statute of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia ("The Statue of the Tribunal"), charges: 1. From about 25 May to about 30 August, 1992, Serb forces collected and confined more than 3,000 Bosnian Muslims and Bosnian Croats from the opstina of Prijedor, Bosnia-Herzegovina, in the former Yugoslavia, in inhumane conditions, under armed guard, in the Omarska "camp", located in a former mining complex approximately fifteen kilometres from the town of Prijedor. As set forth below, the Serb forces killed, raped, sexually assaulted, beat and otherwise mistreated the prisoners at Omarska. Background - Omarska camp: 2.1. In May, 1992, intensive shelling of Muslim areas in the opstina Prijedor caused the Muslim residents to free their homes. The majority of them then surrendered or were captured by Serb forces. As the Serb forces rounded up the Muslims and any Croat residents, they forced the Muslims and Croats to march in columns bound for one or another of the prison camps that the Serbs had established in the opstina. The Serb forces pulled many of the Muslims and Croats from the columns and shot or beat them on the spot. 2.2. On about 25 May 1992, about three weeks after Serbs forcibly took control of government authority in the opstina, and two days after the start of large scale military attacks on Muslim population centres, the Serb forces began taking prisoners to the Omarska camp. 2.3. During the next several weeks, the Serb forces continued to round up Muslims and Croats from Kozarac, Prijedor town, and other places in the opstina and interned them in the camps. Many of Prijedor's Muslim and Croat intellectuals, professional and political leaders were sent to Omarska. There were approximately 40 women in the camp, and all the other prisoners in the camp were men. 2.4. Within the area of the Omarska mining complex that was used for the camp, the camp authorities generally confined the prisoners in three different buildings: the administration building, where interrogations took place and most of the women were confined; the garage or hangar building; the "white house", a small building where particularly severe beatings were administered; and on a cement courtyard area between the buildings known as the "pista". There was another small building, known as the "red house", where prisoners were sometimes taken but most often did not emerge alive. 2.5. Living conditions at Omarska were brutal. Prisoners were crowded together with little or no facilities for personal hygiene. They were fed starvation rations once a day and given only three minutes to get into the canteen area, eat, and get out. The little water they received was ordinarily foul. Prisoners had no changes of clothing and no bedding. They received no medical care. 2.6. Severe beatings were commonplace. The camp guards, and others who came to the camp and physically abused the prisoners, used all manner of weapons during these beatings, including wooden batons, metal rods and tools, lengths of thick industrial cable that had metal balls affixed to the end, rifle butts, and knives. Both female and male prisoners were beaten, tortured, raped, sexually assaulted, and humiliated. In addition to regular beatings and abuse, there were incidents of multiple killings and special terror. Many, whose identities are known and unknown, did not survive the camp. 3. The persons accused in this indictment were commanders, guards and others responsible for the conditions and mistreatment of prisoners in Omarska camp or otherwise assisted the accused.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: 4. Zeljko Meakic also known as (hereinafter aka) Mejakic, aka Meagic, was in charge of Omarska camp beginning in late June, 1992, and was in a position of superior authority to everyone else in the camp. Before he took command of the camp he was chief of security and had full authority over all the guards and any visitors. Before the war began in Bosnia-Herzegovina, he was a police official in Omarska village. 5. Miroslav Kvocka and Dragoljub Prcac were deputies to Zeljko Meakic and were in positions of authority superior to everyone in the camp other than Meakic. For most of the first month of the camp's operation, Kvocka was the commander of the camp. Prior to the start of the war, both Kvocka and Prcac were officials at the Ministry of the Interior in Prijedor. 6. Mladen Radic aka Mlado Radic aka Krkan; Milojica Kos aka Krle; and Momcilo Gruban aka Ckalja were shift commanders who each supervised one of the three shifts of guards that operated the camp. As shift commanders, when they were on duty, they were in positions of superior authority to all the camp personnel, second only to the camp commander and his deputies. 7. The following accused were among those who acted as guards in the Omarska camp: a. Zdravko Govedarica. b. First name unknown Gruban. c. Predrag Kostic aka Kole. d. Nedeljko Paspalj. e. Milan Pavlic. f. Milutin Popovic. g. Drazenko Predojevic. h. Zeljko Savic. 8. In addition to the above-listed accused, who regularly performed duties in Omarska camp, other Serbs entered the camp, subject to the authority of Zeljko Meakic, Miroslav Kvocka, and Dragoljub Prcac, where they killed, beat or otherwise physically abused prisoners. Among those who entered the camp were the following accused: a. Mirko Babic. b. Nikica Janjic. c. Dusan Knezevic aka Duca. d. Dragomir Saponja. f. Zoran Zigic aka Ziga. 8. In addition to the above-listed accused, who regularly performed duties in Omarska camp, other Serbs entered the camp, subject to the authority of Zeljko Meakic, Miroslav Kvocka, and Dragoljub Prcac, where they killed, beat or otherwise physically abused prisoners. Among those who entered the camp were the following accused: a. Mirko Babic. b. Nikica Janjic. c. Dusan Knezevic aka Duca. d. Dragomir Saponja. f. Zoran Zigic aka Ziga. General Allegations: 9. At all times relevant to this indictment, a state of armed conflict and partial occupation existed in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina. 10. All acts or omissions set forth as grave breaches recognised by Article 2 of the Statute of the Tribunal occurred during that armed conflict and partial occupation. 11. All of the prisoners at the Omarska camp, and the Bosnian Muslims and Croats of the opstina of Prijedor referred to in this indictment were, at all relevant times, persons protected by the Geneva Conventions of 1949. 12. All of the accused in the indictment were required to abide by the mandate of the laws and customs governing the conduct of war, including the Geneva Conventions of 1949. 13. Unless otherwise set forth below, all acts and omissions set forth in this indictment took place between 24 May and 30 August 1992. 14. In each paragraph charging torture, the acts were committed by, or at the instigation of, or with the consent or acquiescence of, an official or person acting in an official capacity, and for one or more of the following purposes: to obtain information or a confession from the victim or a third person; to punish the victim for an act the victim or a third person committed or was suspected of having committed; to intimidate or coerce the victim or a third person; and/or for any reason based upon discrimination of any kind. 15. In each paragraph charging crimes against humanity, a crime recognised by Article 5 of the Statute of the Tribunal, the alleged acts or omissions were part of a widespread or large-scale or systematic attack directed against a civilian population specifically the Muslim and Croat population of the Prijedor district. 16. Paragraphs 4 through 15 are re-alleged and incorporated into each of the charges described below. 17. The term "Serb" refers either to Bosnian citizens of Serb descent or to individuals for whom it is unknown whether they were Bosnian Serbs or citizens of Serbia proper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We now go to the counts which relate to the accused, himself. Paragraphs 18.1 through to 22.16 will not be read because these do not involve this particular accused.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 23.1. In about July 1992, Zoran Zigic, Dusan Knezevic and a third unknown person savagely beat Becir Medunjanin on two occasions over a two day period in the "white house". The accused assaulted Becir Medunjanin with a club, a chair --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Are these the accused in the singular or in the plural? No, it is the accused in the plural, thank you. Let us have that correction appear in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: -- a baton and kicked him. The morning after the second assault Becir Medunjanin died in the room and his body was removed from the camp immediately. 23.2. Zoran Zigic and Dusan Knezevic participated in the wilful killing of Becir Medunjanin, a grave breach recognised by Article 2(a) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal, or; 23.3. Alternatively, Zoran Zigic and Dusan Knezevic participated in the murder of Becir Medunjanin, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions. 23.4. Zoran Zigic and Dusan Knezevic participated in the murder of Becir Medunjanin, a crime against humanity recognised by Articles 5(a) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. 24.1. On or about 10 June 1992, Zoran Zigic, Dusan Knezevic, Dragomir Saponja, and Nikica Janjic went to the Omarska camp. Zigic, Knezevic, Saponja, and Janjic were not regular guards at the camp, but were allowed into the camp to murder, beat or otherwise physically abuse the prisoners. On that particular day, they called four prisoners at the Omarska camp, Emir Beganovic, Rezak Hukanovic, Asef Kapetanovic, and Sefik Terzic into the "white house" and severely beat them. The accused used metal batons and cables, a knife, their fists and kicked the victims with their military-style boots. Victim: Emir Beganovic. 24.2. Zoran Zigic, Dusan Knezevic, Dragomir Saponja, and Nikica Janjic participated in wilfully causing serious injury to the body or health of Emir Beganovic, a grave breach recognised by Articles 2(c) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal, or; 24.3. Alternatively, Zoran Zigic, Dusan Knezevic, Dragomir Saponja, and Nikica Janjic participated in subjecting Emir Beganovic to cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions. 24.4. Zoran Zigic, Dusan Knezevic, Dragomir Saponja, and Nikica Janjic participated in subjecting Emir Beganovic to inhumane acts, a crime against humanity recognised by Articles 5(i) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Victim: Rezak Hukanovic. 24.5: Zoran Zigic, Dusan Knezevic, Dragomir Saponja, and Nikica Janjic participated in wilfully causing serious injury to the body or health of Rezak Hukanovic, a grave breach recognised by Articles 2(c) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal, or; 24.6. Alternatively, Zoran Zigic, Dusan Knezevic, Dragomir Saponja, and Nikica Janjic participated in subjecting Rezak Hukanovic to cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions. 24.7. Zoran Zigic, Dusan Knezevic, Dragomir Saponja, and Nikica Janjic participated in subjecting Rezak Hukanovic to inhumane acts, a crime against humanity recognised by Articles 5(i) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Victim: Asef Kapetanovic. 24.8. Zoran Zigic, Dusan Knezevic, Dragomir Saponja, and Nikica Janjic participated in wilfully causing serious injury to the body or health of Asef Kapetanovic, a grave breach recognised by Articles 2(c) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal, or; 24.9. Alternatively, Zoran Zigic, Dusan Knezevic, Dragomir Saponja, and Nikica Janjic participated in subjecting Asef Kapetanovic to cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions. 24.10. Zoran Zigic, Dusan Knezevic, Dragomir Saponja and Nikica Janjic participated in subjecting Asef Kapetanovic to inhumane acts, a crime against humanity recognised by Articles 5(i) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Victim: Sefik Terzic. 24.11. Zoran Zigic, Dusan Knezevic, Dragomir Saponja, and Nikica Janjic participated in wilfully causing serious injury to the body or health of Sefik Terzic, a grave breach recognised by Articles 2(c) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal, or; 24.12. Alternatively, Zoran Zigic, Dusan Knezevic, Dragomir Saponja, and Nikica Janjic participated in subjecting Sefic Terzic to cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions. 24.13. Zoran Zigic, Dusan Knezevic, Dragomir Saponja, and Nikica Janjic participated in subjecting Sefik Terzic to inhumane acts, a crime against humanity recognised by Articles 5(i) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. The remainder of the indictment does not refer to the specific accused. It is signed Richard J Goldstone, Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar, please remain standing. We will ask the accused to rise. Mr. Zigic, will you, please, rise? The Registrar will state each of the counts of the indictment and we will ask you to state to the judges of the Tribunal whether you plead guilty or not guilty to each of these counts. Please express yourself clearly in this respect. Say "I plead guilty" or "I plead not guilty". Madam Registrar, let us begin by count number 1, which is wilful killing.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is in paragraph 23.2, which is alternatively indicated by 23.3. "23.2. Zoran Zigic participated in the wilful killing of Becir Medunjanin, a grave breach recognised by Article 2(a) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal, or; 23.3. Alternatively, Zoran Zigic participated in the murder of Becir Medunjanin, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do you plead guilty or not, Mr. Zigic? THE DEFENDANT: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Paragraph 23.4. Zoran Zigic participated in the murder of Becir Medunjanin a crime against humanity recognised by Articles 5(a) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Zigic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIGIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: As regards the victim Emir Beganovic, this is 24.2 and 24.3, these are the ones with the alternative counts.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Zoran Zigic participated in wilfully causing serious injury to the body or health of Emir Beganovic, a grave breach recognised by Articles 2(c) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal; Or, alternatively, Zoran Zigic, participated in subjecting Emir Beganovic to cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Zigic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIGIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Paragraph 24.4: Zoran Zigic participated in subjecting Emir Beganovic to inhumane acts, a crime against humanity recognised by Articles 5(i) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Zigic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIGIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. Now, let us move to the counts relating to the victim Rezak Hukanovic. These are paragraphs 24.5 through 24.6, which show the alternative counts.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Zoran Zigic participated in wilfully causing serious injury to the body or health or Rezak Hukanovic, a grave breach recognised by Articles 2(c) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal, or; Alternatively, Zoran Zigic, participated in subjecting Rezak Hukanovic to cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Zigic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIGIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Continue.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is now 24.7. Zoran Zigic participated in subjecting Rezak Hukanovic to inhumane acts, a crime against humanity recognised by Articles 5(i) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Zigic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIGIC
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: A count relating to victim, Asef Kapetanovic. This is paragraph 24.8 and 24.9 contains the alternative charges. Zoran Zigic participated in wilfully causing serious injury to the body or health of Asef Kapetanovic, a grave breach recognised by Articles 2(c) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Zigic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIGIC
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Alternatively, Zoran Zigic participated in subjecting Asef Kapetanovic to cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war, recognised by Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal and Articles 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Zigic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIGIC
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 24.10: Zoran Zigic participated in subjecting Asef Kapetanovic to inhumane acts, a crime against humanity recognised by Articles 5(i) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIGIC
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Victim, Sefik Terzic, these are paragraphs 24.11 and 24.12 which have the alternative charges.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Zoran Zigic participated in wilfully causing serious injury to the body or health of Sefik Terzic, a grave breach recognised by Articles 2(c) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal, or; Alternatively, Zoran Zigic participated in subjecting Sefik Terzic to cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Zigic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIGIC
utterances.text: I am not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Paragraph 24.13. Zoran Zigic participated in subjecting Sefik Terzic to inhumane acts, a crime against humanity recognised by Articles 5(i) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Zigic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIGIC
utterances.text: I am not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Zigic. Therefore, you are pleading not guilty to all of the counts in this first indictment; the indictment which you have understood and was read to you in your own language; did you understand the entire translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIGIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The Madam Registrar will note the plea of not guilty of the 15 counts against Mr. Zigic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I will turn to the Prosecutor. It appears that in this case, the Office of the Prosecutor will lodge a request for this case to be referred to another Trial Chamber. Could you give us explanations for that, Mr. Keegan?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. As you are aware, the Prosecutor has submitted a request to have this case, as well as the case of Kvocka and Radic assigned to Trial Chamber II, which currently has charge of the Kovacevic case, because all of the cases relate to or derive from incidents which occurred in the camps in the Prijedor municipality, specifically the Omarska and Keraterm camps. Quite frankly, it is not so much whether it would go to Trial Chamber II or to this Trial Chamber, but the point is that we think that, certainly this case -- the case of Zigic, the accused Zigic -- should be joined with the case of Kvocka and Radic, because, in part, it derives from the same indictment, they are named in the same indictment, the current indictment which was just read. In addition, we would seek then to have the charges under the second indictment relating to Keraterm camp, involving the accused Zigic joined to that case, or heard during the course of that case, (i) for matters of witness issues; (ii) judicial economy, of course, and (iii), the evidence regarding what occurred in the Keraterm camp would be relevant to the legal element of proving that there was a widespread or systematic attack in the Prijedor opstina for purposes of the Article 5 charges against Kvocka and Radic under the Omarska indictment. The Keraterm evidence would be relevant not only to Mr. Zigic, but also to the accused Kvocka and Radic. We would then seek, or bring a motion, before the Trial Chamber to have the evidence, with respect to the cases involving Zigic, Kvocka and Radic, heard concurrently against the accused Kovacevic, who is charged, as I am sure you are aware, your Honours, with a violation of Article 4, complicity in genocide. The bases for the charge of genocide are the events which occurred in the camps in the opstina of Prijedor, as well as the events which occurred during the conflict in general in Prijedor. Many of the witnesses who would be called for the case against Kovacevic are the exact same witnesses who would be called for the cases against Zigic, Radic and Kvocka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The Kovacevic case, when does it begin?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: It is currently scheduled for one week of trial beginning 11th May. Then, it is our understanding that it is tentatively scheduled for the next session to begin in mid-July. It is our submission that if a request was granted it might not result in a delay beyond the one week in May because, if, in fact, the mid-July time frame is accurate, that would be beyond the 60-day time period for preliminary motions for both this accused as well as Kvocka and Radic, who had their initial appearance last week. Therefore, there would be no legal impediment from the Rules to a July trial date for all of the accused; all four of the accused. It is our submission that, at least on the current record, it would only require a delay of one week currently scheduled in July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I would like to turn to Mr. Fourmy, the legal advisor of the Trial Chamber, then to the Defence. Does this fall under the jurisdiction of the Trial Chamber or the Bureau? I think this motion had been given to the President.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: As for information regarding the provisional calendar which has just been distributed and refers to the Kovacevic case, only for the second week of May, which has just been mentioned by the Prosecutor. As regards July, things are still very, very provisional here, as the Prosecutor also said. Yes, you are correct, your Honour, when you said that the motion was lodged with the President of the Tribunal and it does not appear that this Trial Chamber has been seized of this case, since this is a matter which must be discussed further between the Office of the Prosecutor and the judges who will work on the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Fourmy. Do you have any comments, Mr. Fila, you want to make in relation to what the Prosecutor said, or anyone else said so far?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it is in the interests of the accused, Zoran Zigic, that he be tried simultaneously on both indictments. I agree with this part of Mr. Keegan's suggestion. As for the joinder with the Kovacevic case, it is not up to this Defence counsel to stand its views. As far as Mr. Zigic is concerned, it is the same to him, so I have no opinion to voice on this matter. Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. I have understood that there has been a request that either the President of the Tribunal or the Bureau would take the decision and I think that they will not take long to do so. For this part of the hearing, I would just like to recall the obligations which are the Prosecutor's. Whatever Chamber hears this case, you know the provisions of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, specifically, Rule 66, all the different statements and the supporting material which must be brought in. Perhaps it would be unnecessary to try to set up the calendar right now. I think it is a little premature to do so, because if Trial Chamber II is seized after this initial appearance, I think that it would be more appropriate for the President to set the schedule herself. Do you have any further comments you would like to make, Mr. Keegan, as to the calendar?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Just to clarify the record, not just to the calendar. The requests made to the President by the Prosecutor at this stage were only requests to assign both this case and the case of Radic and Kvocka to Trial Chamber II for the initial appearance. We have not specifically requested the joinder or the concurrent presentation of evidence. We believe that that would be a motion for the Trial Chamber. It is my understanding that the request for the assignment of the cases to Trial Chamber II has not occurred. Therefore, as I stated, in point of fact, we made that request only because Trial Chamber II is already seized of Kovacevic which has begun. In point of fact, it matters not, quite frankly, which Trial Chamber gets the cases, only that all the cases are joined for presentation of the evidence. We will be submitting a motion to a Trial Chamber -- either this Chamber or Trial Chamber II, or perhaps both, a joint motion, if you will -- on the issue of joinder, so that whichever Trial Chamber is seized of all of the cases, if we are successful, would then understand the basis for our request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Therefore, I recall that if you ask for this joinder of case with the Kovacevic case you will speak with the President. As far as I am concerned, as regards this accused, the initial appearance took place today in relation to the first indictment. As regards his rights, we have to start now counting the 60 days, because this is a right which is his. Afterwards, another Trial Chamber President has said the date, relating to a joinder of cases, that might change things. If Trial Chamber I keeps this case, I would say that we might set the starting point for the 60 days right now. That is 60 days from today, 20th April, that is until 20th June, in order to fulfil your obligations and to be sure that the Defence is in a position to file its preliminary motions in due time. Do we agree with that, Mr. Fila?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, we agree fully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. If there are no other comments, we will take a five-minute break and I will exceptionally ask Mr. Zigic to remain seated where he is. We will resume in five minutes to take up the second indictment relating to the same accused. The hearing is adjourned.
